diagram_candidates.diagram_kind: affine image schematic; 2D parallelogram plus 3D parallelepiped and rank-one collapse inset
diagram_candidates.rationale: The example compares two invertible linear images whose measure is computed by determinant with a singular map whose image lies on a null line. A diagram can make that geometric contrast immediate.
draw_or_check: Unit square (0,1]^2 mapped by T(x,y)=(2x+y,x+3y), vertices from closure (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1) to (0,0),(2,1),(1,3),(3,4); label determinant and area 5.
Unit cube (0,1]^3 mapped by U(x,y,z)=(2x+y,3y-z,4z); label triangular matrix diagonal (2,3,4), determinant and volume 24.
Singular S(x,y)=(x,x) collapses the square onto {(t,t):0<t<=1}; label rank one and Lebesgue-null line.
Preserve half-open domain conventions; distinguish diagram closures from actual half-open sets.

diagram_candidates.diagram_kind: circle interval map / two-branch interval schematic
diagram_candidates.rationale: The example contrasts inverse-image measure preservation with forward-image measure under a two-branch doubling map. A branch diagram would make the two preimage intervals and endpoint conventions easier to follow.
draw_or_check: Represent the circle as [0,1) with branches [0,1/2) mapped by 2x and [1/2,1) by 2x-1.
Shade the target [0,1/2) and its preimage pieces [0,1/4) and [1/2,3/4), each of length 1/4.
Separately show [0,1/2) mapping forward onto [0,1), preserving the stated distinction between forward and inverse-image measures.
Mark included points 0 and 1/2 and excluded right endpoints 1/4 and 3/4 as stated.
